shipped_row.boundary_rationale: 11:25 and 11:26 both carry the noun ברכה ("blessing", oshb:Prov.11.25, skeleton tier; oshb:Prov.11.26, skeleton tier): 11:25 calls the generous person a נפש ברכה ("soul of blessing") who will be made fat, and 11:26 promises ברכה ("blessing") on the head of one who sells rather than withholds grain — both verses argue the same behavior pattern (giving/selling versus withholding) and its reward under that one shared noun. A skeleton-level substring sweep of ברכה returns 3 verses book-wide (the third is Prov.10.7, non-adjacent), and this pair alone stands adjacent among them; the three hits are not one uniform word-form — the noun surfaces bare at 11:25 (בְּרָכָ֥ה, oshb:Prov.11.25), and prefixed at 10:7 (לִבְרָכָ֑ה, oshb:Prov.10.7) and 11:26 (וּ֝בְרָכָ֗ה, oshb:Prov.11.26). A different, construct-state spelling of the same root, found separately at Prov.10.22, Prov.11.11, and Prov.24.25, is not counted in that figure.
shipped_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading 11:25 and 11:26 as unrelated separate proverbs was set aside given both the noun's rarity and the shared giving/withholding behavior pattern; extending the cluster into 11:24 or 11:27 was rejected, since neither carries the ברכה (oshb:Prov.11.26) noun.

shipped_row.boundary_rationale: Both verses carry the exact same plural noun for fools -- כְּ֝סִילִ֗ים (oshb:Prov.13.19) and כְסִילִ֣ים (oshb:Prov.13.20), byte tier -- both inside their own complete antithesis: fulfilled desire is sweet to the soul while fools despise turning from evil (13:19), and one who walks with the wise grows wise while a companion of fools comes to harm (13:20). As with the tongue-noun pairing at Prov.12.18-Prov.12.19, the grouping rests on one repeated content token bridging two independently closed couplets rather than on a continuing construction, so the evidence is thin by the same standard.
shipped_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Keeping these as separate stand-alone rows was the default and was reconsidered chiefly because of the repeated fools-noun; since that is one shared token rather than a construction run, the cluster call carries the same reduced confidence as the thin catchword pairing at Prov.12.18-Prov.12.19.

shipped_row.boundary_rationale: Abundant food sits in the A-colon's tillage, whose owner is named with the plural noun רָאשִׁ֑ים (oshb:Prov.13.23, byte tier), ordinarily meaning heads or chiefs -- WEB renders it poor people, a gloss not transparent from the bare consonants as staged here. The waw turns to a sweeping-away for lack of justice, so whichever sense the disputed noun carries, the sentence's shape (abundance existing, then lost to injustice) is one sustained thought rather than a subject-vs-subject antithesis.
shipped_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Resolving the disputed noun's sense before deciding the boundary was set aside as unnecessary: no morphology layer is staged for this extract, and the verse's one-sentence shape does not depend on which sense is preferred.
